data.theme: Leadership Competencies and Self-Efficacy in Engineering
data.definition: The development and validation of instruments to measure engineering students' leadership self-efficacy, including the identification of key leadership domains relevant to engineering contexts. This theme also examines the relationship between leadership confidence and broader professional competencies.

data.theme: Writing Attitudes and Affective Dimensions in Engineering Education
data.definition: The study of engineering students' attitudes, emotions, and apprehensions related to academic and professional writing, including the development of tools to assess and address writing challenges. This theme explores the impact of writing attitudes on career trajectories and educational outcomes.

The measurement of engineering students' confidence in performing specific tasks within biomedical engineering contexts, such as problem identification, engineering solutions, and grant proposal writing. This theme emphasizes the clinical and technical relevance of self-efficacy assessments.

The examination of how psychological constructs (e.g., self-efficacy, motivation, attitudes) influence educational and career outcomes in engineering students. This theme includes the validation of instruments to measure these constructs and their predictive validity for persistence, academic success, and career intentions.
